hero.title: ProyectoEspaña.dev
hero.slogan:
Equip the Sentinels!
So the world knows!

contacto.texto: One single contact email address for everything: Sentinel applications, offers of gear or technical help, and any question about how the project works. It is answered from there.

campanas.titulo: There are no active campaigns yet
campanas.texto: This is where the crowdfunding campaigns will appear: one per Sentinel, with the gear it asks for — smart glasses, a drone, a thermal camera, an antenna —, what coverage it is for and what it costs. None is open yet, ProyectoEspaña.dev has only just started.

p1.texto: ProyectoEspaña.dev is a private initiative that equips the people who document what happens on Spanish soil and tell the world about it.

p2.texto: Ceuta, the Valencia flash floods, storm Filomena, the La Palma volcano. Events the world needs to see in detail and as they happen, not three days later, summarised or bent to keep certain powers happy.

p3.texto: You have to move fast, and you cannot broadcast with a phone in your hand. At night you see nothing without a thermal camera. What you need to show is far away, or moving, or you need to be able to leave quickly. Sometimes the place is not safe and there is no vehicle to leave in.

p4.texto: Gear that frees your hands and survives the terrain, training to use it well, and a technical organisation that coordinates broadcasting, storage and distribution.

p5.texto: Through crowdfunding campaigns. Each one states what gear it needs, for whom and what for.

p1.texto: People who already tell what is happening. They have their own community on social media and a provable track record documenting events with their own means.

p2.texto: At least 10,000 followers on one platform and a public history of coverage on the ground. The figure is not a gate: the track record counts more than the number.

p3.texto: The gear the campaign funded, as their own property. It is not a loan and there is nothing to give back: it is theirs and they will keep using it once the campaign ends.

p4.texto: Nothing forces a Sentinel to deliver except the thing they value most: their credibility. Everything is public, and anyone who takes gear from a campaign and does not use it does so in front of their own community. That is why a track record is required: the gear goes to people who already have a reputation to protect. And if something gets in the way, an accident or an illness, that is misfortune, not deceit.

p1.texto: Who you are, where you publish and the community you have. Links to coverage you have already done on the ground. And what gear you are missing to tell it better.

p2.texto: The public track record is what counts: what you have covered, with what means and in front of whom. If the application fits, you get an answer at the same contact email address.

p3.texto: If it goes ahead, a campaign opens in your name: what gear it needs, for whom and what for. It is funded by those who want what happens in the world to be made known.

p4.texto: Send an email to the address shown below, with the subject “Sentinel application”. No forms and no middlemen.
